claims.proposition_evaluated: The $100 million approved for bike lanes (capital profile CM-20-0330, Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3, $100,000 thousand over 2023-2026 as approved December 2022) is almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget, with the denominator fixed to the printed cell 'Expenditure & Transfers, 2022 Budget' in the Snow and Ice Control program summary of the Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, and 'almost double' meaning a ratio of at least 1.8 (Supported), 1.5 to below 1.8 (Partially supported), below 1.5 (Contradicted).
claims.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY: the printed cell is $64,466 (in $000s), Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Parks & Roads Services, Program Summary, Snow and Ice Control, row 'Expenditure & Transfers', column '2022 Budget', printed page 212 (PDF page 216). Ratio 100,000/64,466 = 1.551 -> Partially supported under the primary cutoffs (1.5 to <1.8; the failing part is the word 'double', the figure is about 1.55 times, or 'half again'). Under the alternative cutoffs (Supported >=1.7; Partially 1.25 to <1.7) also Partially supported. Same page: row 'Revenue & Transfers' $13, 'Intra-municipal Recoveries' ($800), 'Total Net Operating Requirement' $63,653 (2022). ALTERNATIVE A (cell plus every council amendment to the 2022 Snow and Ice Control budget in force on 2022-12-12): I found three council-approved 2022 additions, all one-time: (1) 2022-03-14, City Council, carry-forward of $2.3 million of 2021 Snow and Ice Control surplus into 2022 (recorded in the Spring 2022 SOBA report FCS01143 as 'approved by Council on March 14, 2022'); (2) 2022-04-19, City Council, Spring 2022 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment FCS01143 Attachment 1, 'Enhanced Snow Clearing Pilot costs (total costs of $16.6 M, less $2.3M from 2021 program surplus...)', +$14,300 thousand expense funded from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, motion carried 13-0; (3) 2022-07-04, City Council item CO01277, 'That the Parks and Roads Services Branch budget be increased by $4.7 million, from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, on a one time basis to fund the Snow and Ice Control program for the 2022 portion of the upcoming winter season', carried 13-0. The Fall 2021 SOBA (FCS, November 2021) contains no Snow and Ice Control change to the 2022 budget. Alternative A = 64,466 + 2,300 + 14,300 + 4,700 = $85,766 thousand; ratio 1.166 -> Contradicted under the primary cutoffs (<1.5) and Contradicted under the alternative cutoffs (<1.25). Cross-check: the City's own year-end 'Snow and Ice Control' 2022 adjusted expense budget in the Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022 (FCS01656 Attachment 1, page 38 of the PDF, in $000s) is $79,474 (revenue budget $23,108, net budget ($56,366)); on that figure the ratio is 1.258 -> Contradicted under the primary cutoffs, Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs (1.25 to <1.7). If only the 2022-07-04 amendment is counted (the reading the brief named), 64,466 + 4,700 = 69,166, ratio 1.446 -> Contradicted (primary cutoffs), Partially supported (alternative cutoffs). ALTERNATIVE B (2023 Budget): the cell the brief names does not exist: the City's 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans contains no Snow and Ice Control program summary table; the Parks and Roads Services branch section lists Snow and Ice Control only as a service description and the enhanced-standards service package. Council's December 2022 Operating Budget Amendment 18 (carried 12-1, M. Janz opposed) funded the 'Enhanced Snow and Ice Control Service Standards' package at 20 per cent: 2023 $274,600 (Community Standards and Neighbourhoods) and $3,768,000 (Parks and Roads Services); 2024 $3,724,800; 2025 $2,476,800; 2026 $721,400; the printed service package table (2023-2026 Operating Budget, page 105) shows $4,043 (2023), $3,725 (2024), $2,477 (2025), $721 (2026) in $000s. The closest City-published 2023 snow budget figure is the Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2023 (FCS02229 Attachment 1, supplemental page 1 of 7): Snow and Ice Control 2023 expense budget $63,574 thousand (actual $54,917; net budget ($61,173), net actual ($52,555)); this is the budget as adjusted at year-end, not the December 2022 approved figure. Media reported the December 2022 approved 2023 total as $60.9 million (Global News 2022-12-20; CBC 2022-12-16: base $56.9 million plus $4 million). Ratios: 100,000/63,574 = 1.573 and 100,000/60,900 = 1.642 -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets. NET AND ACTUAL CONTEXT (not denominators): printed 2022 Total Net Operating Requirement $63,653 thousand -> 1.571; City year-end 2022 adjusted net budget ($56,366) -> 1.774; 2022 actual Snow and Ice Control expense $97,571 thousand (net actual ($74,607)), Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022 -> 1.025 on actual. DEFINITION SENSITIVITY: the verdict is Partially supported on the primary cell but Contradicted on the budget as amended in-year (Alternative A); the finding is definition-sensitive and neither side can cite it without that qualification. The three one-time 2022 additions were extraordinary responses to a bad winter and a residential blading pilot; the ongoing base budget (printed cell, or the 2023 approved figure) gives 1.55 to 1.64 either way. QUOTATION CONTEXT: the advocacy page (live 2026-09-02; Wayback Machine availability API confirms a capture at 2022-12-12 05:58:23 UTC) reads 'In fact, it's almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget!' and 'the $100 million he wants to spend on Bike Lanes is almost 5 times the amount he wants to spend on affordable housing'; the page names no snow figure. Context only: the December 2022 affordable housing land amendment reported by CBC was $22.9 million (100/22.9 = 4.4x) and Table 8's 'Affordable Housing and Homelessness Service' 2023-2026 capital line is $49.2 million (2.0x).

claims.suggested_one_line: On the City's printed 2022 snow-clearing budget ($64.5 million), the $100 million bike-lane program is about 1.55 times, not almost double; on the 2022 budget as topped up in-year it is not even 1.2 times.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Council approved $100 million over 2023-2026 for capital profile CM-20-0330. The Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget prints the 2022 Snow and Ice Control expenditure budget at $64.466 million, so the ratio is 1.55: well above a year of snow clearing, but 'double' overstates it (Partially supported). Council added $2.3 million, $14.3 million and $4.7 million to the 2022 snow budget in March, April and July 2022, taking it to about $85.8 million (ratio 1.17), and the City actually spent $97.6 million on snow and ice in 2022. The approved 2023 snow budget was about $60.9 to $63.6 million (ratio 1.57 to 1.64). Like for like, the program's 2023 allocation ($5.95 million) was about a tenth of the 2023 snow budget, and the whole $100 million is about 38 per cent of four years of snow budgets. Through December 31, 2025 the City had spent $40.0 million of the program.
suggested_tldr: $100 million (CM-20-0330, 2023-2026) vs printed 2022 snow budget $64.466 million: ratio 1.55, Partially supported.
Counting council's three one-time 2022 top-ups ($21.3 million) the ratio falls to 1.17; 2022 actual snow spending was $97.6 million.
Per year, the bike program ($25 million average approved; $13.3 million average actually spent 2023-2025) is well below the roughly $63 to 68 million annual snow budget.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In the City's adopted 2023-2026 Capital Budget, roads get $1.8 billion, about eighteen times the $100 million for bike lanes (CM-20-0330), where 'roads' is the sum of 2023-2026 approved amounts (Appendix A, $000s) of every capital profile whose sheet carries Service Category 'Roads' or 'Neighbourhood Renewal', excluding 21-20-2100 and 14-66-2570 and adding bridge profiles 23-24-0300, 21-24-9301 and 21-24-9302; Supported if the total is at least $1.5 billion, Partially supported from $1.0 billion, Contradicted below $1.0 billion.
claims.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY BOUNDARY, verified against every profile sheet (I parsed the 'Service Category:' field on all 161 profile sheets in the adopted document): 20 sheets carry 'Roads' and 11 carry 'Neighbourhood Renewal'; the membership matches the editor's reading exactly, and the three bridge profiles carry no Service Category as the brief says. Amounts (2023-2026 total, $000s, Appendix A page): ROADS: 18-66-6503 50 Street CPR Grade Separation 94,202 (p.103); 19-22-9006 Terwillegar Drive Expressway Upgrades - Alternate Staging 119,200 + 41,821 = 161,021 (both lines, p.104); 21-20-9301 Yellowhead Trail 156 Street to St Albert Trail 54,634 (p.104); 21-20-9302 Yellowhead Trail Fort Road Widening 54,597 (p.104); 21-40-9031 Winterburn Industrial Road Upgrading 12 (p.104); 21-40-9032 Mistatim/Southeast Industrial Road Upgrading 10 (p.103); 22-22-9700 124 Street 109 to 118 Avenue 10,056 (p.102); 22-22-9701 Gateway Blvd Renewal 5,094 (p.103); CM-20-2020 Transportation Planning and Design - Growth 9,007 (p.104); CM-22-0000 Goods Movement - Arterial Renewal 64,843 (p.104); CM-24-0000 Bridges & Auxiliary Structures - Renewal 209,836 (p.104); CM-26-0000 Traffic Systems - Renewal 9,308 (p.104); CM-66-2194 Regulated Safety Upgrades at Railway Crossings 720 (p.104); CM-66-2525 Traffic Signals - Developer and ARA Funded 16,000 (p.104); CM-66-2585 Safe Crossings 25,875 (p.101); CM-66-2596 Safe and Livable Community Streets 17,148 (p.101); CM-99-0060 Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion: Project Development 7,914 (p.104); CM-99-9600 Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion: Project Delivery 376,255 (p.104); subtotal Roads 1,116,532. NEIGHBOURHOOD RENEWAL (all p.101): 20-40-9017 4,658; 20-40-9019 721; 21-40-9023 14,652; 21-40-9024 22,047; 21-40-9025 9,780; 21-40-9026 2,100; 21-40-9027 464; 22-40-9028 17,130; 22-40-9029 23,710; CM-25-0000 Transportation: Neighbourhoods - Renewal 545,717; CM-27-0000 Neighbourhood Alley Renewal 81,310; subtotal 722,289. BRIDGES (p.103): 23-24-0300 High Level Bridge Rehabilitation 97,000; 21-24-9301 Latta Bridge Replacement 9,832; 21-24-9302 Glenora Bridge Renewal 50; subtotal 106,882. PRIMARY TOTAL 1,945,703 ($1,945.7 million), ratio to $100 million = 19.46 -> Supported under the primary cutoffs (>= $1.5 billion) and under the alternative cutoffs (>= $1.62 billion). REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE: Table 8 'Adopted Capital Budget by Service', page 56, 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' 2023-2026: Growth 622.8, Renewal 1,171.2, Total $1,794.0 million (2027 and beyond 108.6; overall 1,902.6); ratio 17.94 -> Supported under both cutoff sets. This line is the combined service allocation including CM-20-0330 and other active-pathway funding; it is not a roads total. NARROWEST (Service Category 'Roads' only): $1,116.5 million, 11.17x -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets (the failing part is the figure). WIDEST (primary plus 21-50-9101 103 Avenue Streetscape 560, 21-50-9100 103A Avenue Pedway 25,400, 17-74-4103 Jasper Avenue New Vision Phase 2 265, CM-20-3102 Chinatown Infrastructure Improvements 10,100, CM-20-3100 Missing and Enhanced Sidewalk Connections 13,615, 20-20-2024 Edmonton-Strathcona County Pedestrian Bridge 30,205; extras 80,145): $2,025.8 million, 20.26x -> Supported. Sheets whose label differs from the editor's reading: none. Two profiles with blank Service Category that a reader might expect under roads were not included under any reading, per the brief: CM-29-0000 Transportation - Minor Renewal Program (15,000, p.104) and 21-31-9100 Rundle Park Road and Parking Lot Renewal (181, p.104). ADDITIONAL SENSITIVITY, reported not carrying the verdict: the four Yellowhead Trail profiles (CM-99-9600, CM-99-0060, 21-20-9301, 21-20-9302; 493,400 combined) carry Service Category 'Roads' on their sheets but Table 8 reports them as the transformational project 'Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion' ($493.4 million), outside 'Active Pathways and Roads Service'. Removing them from the primary gives $1,452.3 million, 14.5x -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets; removing them from the narrowest gives $623.1 million, 6.2x -> Contradicted. THE '180': Global News (2022-12-12, Stephanie Swensrude) quotes Councillor Janz: 'Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.' $1.8 billion is 18 times $100 million, not 180; the figure appears only in that article; the council minutes do not record debate speech, and no other coverage I found repeats the sentence with either number. The councillor's own campaign page states 'The $100M represents half a percent of the $1.8 Billion dollar capital budget over the same period', which is also arithmetically wrong (it is 5.6 per cent); it confirms the $1.8 billion figure is the councillor's, and that figure matches Table 8's 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' total of $1,794.0 million. QUALIFICATION 2 (as amended): a roads-only as-amended total cannot be computed from published documents because composite renewal profiles (CM-25-0000, CM-24-0000, CM-22-0000) are split into standalone project profiles as work is approved and the City publishes no roads total; the whole-budget trajectory is: tax-supported 2023-2026 capital budget $9,073 million after 2022 carry-forwards (Fall 2024 SCBA Attachment 1); Spring 2024 SCBA approved 2024-06-11 (CBC: capital budget increased to $10.4 billion); Fall 2024 SCBA approved 2024-12-02, net +$151.8 million tax-supported; Fall 2025 SCBA 2025-11-24, net +$98.2 million, total capital budget after Fall 2025 SCBA $11,612 million (all years); final adjustment 2026-06-16, +$126.6 million (1.10%) on an $11.56 billion capital budget (City webpage). limitations: The roads-only total is definition-dependent: $1,945.7 million (primary), $1,794.0 million (Table 8 combined service line, includes active pathways), $2,025.8 million (widest), $1,116.5 million (narrowest, Partially supported); the Yellowhead Trail profiles ($493.4 million) sit inside the primary because their sheets say 'Roads' although Table 8 reports them as a transformational project.

Every included profile is counted in full; CM-25-0000 Neighbourhood Renewal ($545.7 million) and CM-24-0000 bridges ($209.8 million) fund sidewalks, alleys and structures as well as roadway, and the City publishes no roadway share.

The 'roads total as amended to the as-of date' cannot be computed from published documents; I report the whole-budget trajectory and the current approved budgets of the largest roads profiles instead.
Roads capital expenditure by year is not published by service; only profile-level to-date actuals for projects over $20 million are available, so qualification 3 is partial.
The '180 times' wording is known only from the Global News article; council minutes do not transcribe debate, and I did not review council video.

The profile named in the minutes ('Bike Plan Implementation - Approach 3') and in the budget document ('Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3') is the same profile number, CM-20-0330.

claims.suggested_one_line: On the City's own profile labels, roads-category and neighbourhood-renewal capital in the 2023-2026 budget totals about $1.95 billion, roughly 19 times the $100 million bike-lane program; the combined 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line the councillor likely used is $1.79 billion.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Summing every capital profile the City labels 'Roads' or 'Neighbourhood Renewal' in the adopted 2023-2026 Capital Budget, plus three vehicle-carrying bridge rehabilitations, gives $1,945.7 million, about 19 times the $100 million approved for CM-20-0330. The budget's Table 8 shows 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' at $1,794.0 million, which includes the bike program itself and is the figure closest to the councillor's $1.8 billion. Read narrowly (profiles labelled 'Roads' only) the total is $1.12 billion, about 11 times. The councillor's '180 times' does not follow from $1.8 billion and $100 million, which are 18 times apart. Through December 31, 2025 the City had spent $40.0 million of the bike program's $99.6 million current budget.
suggested_tldr: Roads-only 2023-2026 approved capital under the City's labels: $1,945.7 million, 19.5 times $100 million (Supported).
Table 8's combined 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line is $1,794.0 million (17.9 times) and includes the bike program.
'180 times' is a misstatement; $1.8 billion is 18 times $100 million. Narrowest reading ('Roads' label only): $1.12 billion, 11 times.
